kind.description: "pr" waits for a GitHub pull request: its checks or its merge (see `until`); "worker" waits for workers you own; "request" waits for replies to requests you sent; "peer" waits for named peer tasks to message you or settle; "timer" wakes you after `seconds`; "process" wakes you when a background command ends.

operation_id.description: Optional retry identity. Reuse it with exactly the same arguments after an unknown outcome; never use it for a different registration.

pr.description: kind "pr": the HTTPS GitHub pull request URL.

until.description: kind "pr": "checks" (default) watches checks; "merge" waits for merge or closure and ignores queue removal. After requesting a merge, use "merge_or_blocked": wakes on merge, closure, conflict, or neither queue membership nor enabled auto-merge remaining. Pending checks or a queue slot alone do not end it. All targets retain their deadline and query-error exits. Only "merged" confirms success; "blocked" requires inspection and grants no permission to retry or merge.

wake_on_conflict.description: kind "pr": Default true for "checks" and "merge". Set false when your work depends on another PR merging and you want to ignore its conflicts. "merge_or_blocked" always reports conflicts, regardless of this setting. With "checks", a conflicting PR may have no checks, ending as no_checks or deadline.

head_sha.description: kind "pr": optional. Right after you push, pass the pushed commit (`git rev-parse HEAD`): the wait watches it while GitHub still shows the previous head, for up to 60 seconds.

worker_ids.description: kind "worker": the workers you own to wait for (1–32 unique ids).

request_ids.description: kind "request": the requests you sent, to a worker, your parent or a peer task, to wait for a reply to (1–32 unique ids).

peer_ids.description: kind "peer": the peer root tasks of this project to wait for (1–32 unique task ids; find them with `hsq message tasks`). A message from one of them, or one of them settling, ends the wait; other messages wake you and keep it open.

mode.description: kind "worker" or "request": "any" wakes you when one selected id settles (default), "all" when every one has, "one" takes exactly one id.

timeout_seconds.description: The deadline in seconds. kind "pr": 1–7200, default 1800. kind "worker", "request" or "peer": 1–7200, default 600 (the default shown is the pr one). kind "process": 1–7200, default 1800.

pid.description: kind "process": the PID of the background command: the `pid` the job start command printed.

exit_file.description: kind "process": optional. The `exitFile` that `hsq job start` printed for this `pid`, in any `--dir`, or a file that your own wrapper writes the exit code to, in $TMPDIR or the worktree, with a new name for each command. Leave it out for a command that is already running or that writes its status file somewhere else.

note.description: kind "timer" or "process": what to re-check, handed back to you at the wake.
